I installed it yesterday, in sys mode with LVM over LUKS. Took a few tries to get the install working, had to chroot in and regenerate the initramFS.

After that I had problems getting Xorg working, it seemed that Nouveau failed to recognize my GTX 750. Threw an old 8800GT in which worked with no issues. After that, everything has been great!

I wish the repos were larger, but at least they are up-to-date. Thinking of making some packages for XULrunner, Conkeror browser, Worker file-manager, Pinta or Krita, etc. With some more people adding and maintaining packages this distro could turn into something really great.

I used the instructions from the bottom half of this page (note, it failed the first time through, probably my own fault, chrooted in and rebuilt initramFS, only other problem is that during installation the drive I installed to was detected as /dev/sde and upon boot was /dev/sda, so I had to modify the cryptroot= line in Syslinux file extlinux.conf):

http://wiki.alpinelinux.org/wiki/LVM_on_LUKS

I personally experienced at least one, maybe two hauntings or sightings. The first took place back in early Spring of 1999. My wife and I had just purchased our house, but we were still living in our apartment waiting for the closing date to approach. We didn't have much furniture to fill the house so we decided to take advantage of opportunities that may arise from the time we bought the house to the closing date to obtain good quality furniture on the cheap. A colleague of ours experienced the unfortunate loss of her father back in March and she was going to sell their family home as well as her father's possessions. Knowing we had just purchased a house she invited us over to the family home to have first picks at any furniture before she held a garage sale. We agreed and went over to the house that weekend. The inside of the house was almost bare of large furniture and all photos were packed away. She led us to her father's study and I saw a great dresser of solid wood. She sold me the dresser along with a rattan bookcase for a great price. We took the dresser and the bookcase back to our apartment and simply placed them in the living room since we were going to start packing for our move in a couple of days. Our apartment was a simple one bedroom with our bedroom door facing the kitchen. I remember waking up at around 2 a.m. with an urgent need to go to the bathroom. I opened the bedroom door and stepped into the hallway. It was dark except to my left I noticed a silvery light. I thought at first it was moonlight, but as I turned to look I noticed it was a head of an old man floating above the dresser I just purchased. It didn't say anything to me, it just turned and looked at me. I must have stood there for about a minute before my body reminded me why I woke up. I remember feeling numb and simply going to the washroom as though I was on auto pilot. It wasn't till I was done and having washed my hands and face that my brain registered what I just saw. My first thought was "What the fuck was that?!". Then I remember shaking and standing at the bathroom door looking at the door knob and wondering wildly what may be waiting for me on the other side. I mustered up the courage to open the door and entered a dark hallway. I looked over to where the dresser stood and it was dark; no moonlight, no ambient light from outside. I rushed back to bed and tried not to think about what I experienced. I eventually fell back to sleep and told my wife what happened in the morning. I still can't explain what I experienced nor why I experienced it.

Experience #2: When my wife and I moved into our house we were told by a neighbour that the previous owner had passed away from a heart attack while mowing the lawn. I didn't give it much thought until my wife and I both noticed that at night there would be a shadow cast on our lawn in the shape of a standing man. The first time we noticed was when we drove up to our driveway, noticed the shadow and thought someone was standing at our back door. However there was no one at the back door. Yes it could have been the flood lights casting a shadow through the bush or our mulberry tree, but the shape of the rose bush and the position of the mulberry tree wouldn't have cast that shadow. Even after changing the bulbs, the shadow continued to be cast. This lasted for about a year and then it stopped.

Experience #3 This happened to my mother and brother. When I was a teenager, my family lived in WWII era bungalow. It was small and cozy and suited us fine. My father worked night shifts and so he slept most of the day. He told us that he had a hard time sleeping in this house and felt like someone was always in the room with him while he tried to sleep. My parents eventually bought a new house and it was during one night when my mother and brother were packing things up in the old house that they experienced something odd. I was working that night and so it was just the two of them packing. They told me that every room they entered and started packing the lights in that room would suddenly go off and wouldn't come back on. They checked the fuses and everything seemed fine.

Those are my experiences.

I don't think I would count GNU/Linux as an anti-malware solution. But I would count ClamAV for GNU/Linux OS's.

TBH I have only used the anti-malware solutions that are build into the OS for quite some time. Windows 7+ (I think is when it started) had the option of installing windows defender. There is also a firewall built in.

They are way lighter than any other anti-malware software, and as long as you're using a sandboxed web browser and not running *.exe email attachments you should be fine.

On OS X I don't use anything, I just keep the 'applications must be signed' enabled. On an app to app basis, I'll let unsigned apps run, but in general if it's not signed, I don't run it.

On Linux... well it's Linux. When I'm on Linux I'm usually doing everything from source, so I don't worry about it at all.

MS Defender (MS Security Essentials on Windows 7 and lower) is actually relatively insecure as compared to most premium A/V solutions. As compared here:

http://www.av-test.org/en/compare-manufacturer-results/

And here:

http://chart.av-comparatives.org/chart1.php (The white dotted line is MSE/Windows Defender)
meh. I tend to agree with this guy when he says AV Software is dead.

Malwarebytes is what I use more than anything. I don't have a Firewall installed because I normally VPN to everything. I'm using Bitdefender for Anti-Virus because I like that it has a "Gaming Mode" where it detects when I'm playing a game and goes into a lower priority mode.

SuperAntiSpyware has been good for most of a decade. TBH I think it's better than MWB lately. It's worth a try.

In terms of best detection and removal overall? HitMan Pro is great but the trial is very limiting and I don't really trust "cloud" based scanners.
